text:
rhea: Heads-up Enterprise prospect (Neptune Health) requires per-tenant model pinning (exact model binary + quantization) with an SLA that pinned model outputs remain stable for 6 months. Sales (samir) says it's a blocker for pilot. This affects rollout and storage. Need quick call on whether to include in public v1.

samir: Theyre explicit: no model drift allowed for clinical review. They will pay for dedicated capacity if we support pinning, otherwise they wont run the pilot.

mateo: Engineering note: per-tenant pinning means we must: store additional model artifacts, extend routing to honor tenant pins, and ensure KV-cache compatibility across pinned vs default variants. Ballpark: 23w infra work + 1w validation. Also increases CI matrix.

arun: Serving runtime concerns: pinned models block some of our automatic kernel selection and quantization suggestions. We can allow pinned "snapshots" but then we lose some cost/latency optimizations. Need to surface that to sales/customers.

gloria: Product: if we add pinning to v1, it complicates rollout and our rollback story. Alternative is "signed snapshot" add-on: we deliver a certified snapshot under SOW and guarantee stability for a contract term. That keeps public v1 simpler.

rhea: Option A: Fold lightweight pinning into public v1 (tenant pin points to a saved model variant, basic admin UI). Likely slide v1 by ~1 week for validation. Option B: Keep v1 focused on single global model routing, deliver pinned-snapshot as paid add-on (SOW) with dedicated capacity. Option C: Provide an interim 'model-freeze' checkbox for pilots — manual process with ops-runbook.

mateo: Pro/con quick take:
- A: Good for wider enterprise adoption but increases QA and storage cost, risk of rollout complexity.
- B: Keeps milestone, revenue via SOW, predictable.
- C: Fastest short-term but ops-intensive and not scalable.

samir: Neptune would accept B if offering a clear timeline and a signed snapshot SLA. Theyre ok with dedicated capacity cost.

arun: If we choose B, we need an RFC that defines artifact signing, retrieval semantics, and monitoring to detect accidental drift (checksums + smoke tests). I can specify tests in 3 days.

gloria: UX + docs: we should be explicit: "Pinned snapshots are an enterprise add-on; GA model routing remains generally recommended." Will draft comms and a customer-facing decision table.

rhea: Draft checklist (quick):
```
Public v1 (keep):
- single global model routing + model catalog
- per-tenant config limited to routing, quotas
- telemetry + canary rollouts

Enterprise snapshot add-on (SOW):
- artifact signing + delivery of pinned model snapshot
- dedicated capacity or tenant isolations
- SLA for snapshot immutability + audit logs
- onboarding runbook + validation tests
```

mateo: Ops note: If we take C (manual freeze) we need an on-call rotation for snapshot pushes and a runbook; acceptable only for 1-2 pilots.

samir: Sales action: Il confirm Neptune prefers the SOW snapshot path and will price accordingly.

arun: Il draft the artifact/signing RFC and include validation tests by EOD next Tue.

gloria: Il prepare the customer decision table and a short FAQ for sales by Fri.

ops-bot: Calendar: "Neptune snapshot scoping" set for 2026-04-02 09:00 PT. Invite sent.

rhea: Quick vote: :thumbsup: for Option B (snapshot SOW + keep v1 date); :thumbsdown: fold pinning into v1 and delay. React in-thread.

mateo: :thumbsup:

arun: :thumbsup:

gloria: :thumbsup:

samir: :thumbsup: (sales aligned with SOW)

rhea: Consensus leaning to snapshot SOW. Il update milestone tracker and mark "model pinning" as enterprise add-on. Thanks team.
